questions.question: What is the basic unit of life?
questions.correctAnswer: The cell
questions.explanation: Every living thing - from a bacterium to a whale - is built from cells, and every life process happens inside cells or between them.
questions.memoryHook: Cells are the building blocks of life.

questions.question: Which organelle is known as the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.correctAnswer: The mitochondria
questions.explanation: Mitochondria release energy from food through cellular respiration.
questions.memoryHook: Mitochondria make the cell's energy.

questions.question: Which structure controls what enters and leaves a cell?
questions.correctAnswer: The cell membrane
questions.explanation: The cell membrane is selectively permeable, controlling what passes in and out.
questions.memoryHook: The cell membrane is the cell's gatekeeper.

questions.question: Where is DNA stored in a eukaryotic cell?
questions.correctAnswer: In the nucleus
questions.explanation: The nucleus holds the cell's DNA, the instructions for making proteins.
questions.memoryHook: The nucleus is the cell's instruction manual.

questions.question: Which organelle makes proteins?
questions.correctAnswer: The ribosome
questions.explanation: Ribosomes read mRNA and assemble amino acids into proteins.
questions.memoryHook: Ribosomes build proteins.

questions.question: Which organelle performs photosynthesis in plant cells?
questions.correctAnswer: The chloroplast
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts capture sunlight to make food in photosynthesis.
questions.memoryHook: Chloroplasts turn sunlight into food.

questions.question: What is the main difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
questions.correctAnswer: Prokaryotic cells have no nucleus; eukaryotic cells do
questions.explanation: Prokaryotes, like bacteria, lack a membrane-bound nucleus; eukaryotes have one.
questions.memoryHook: No nucleus means prokaryote.

questions.question: What does the Golgi apparatus do?
questions.correctAnswer: It modifies, sorts, and packages proteins
questions.explanation: The Golgi receives newly made proteins from the ER in small vesicles, adds finishing touches such as sugar tags, then sorts and ships them to their destinations.
questions.memoryHook: The Golgi is the cell's post office.

questions.question: Which organelle breaks down waste and old cell parts?
questions.correctAnswer: The lysosome
questions.explanation: Lysosomes contain enzymes that digest waste and worn-out organelles.
questions.memoryHook: Lysosomes are the cell's cleanup crew.

questions.question: What is the fluid that fills a cell?
questions.correctAnswer: Cytoplasm
questions.explanation: Cytoplasm is a gel of water, salts, and proteins; its watery part, the cytosol, is where many of the cell's chemical reactions take place.
questions.memoryHook: Cytoplasm is the cell's jelly.

questions.question: Which structure is found in plant cells but not in animal cells?
questions.correctAnswer: The cell wall
questions.explanation: The cell wall lies outside the membrane and is woven from cellulose fibers, giving plant cells a fixed shape and extra protection that animal cells do not have.
questions.memoryHook: Plant cells wear a stiff wall; animal cells do not.

questions.question: What is the function of the rough endoplasmic reticulum?
questions.correctAnswer: To make and fold proteins
questions.explanation: Ribosomes on its surface start building proteins, and those proteins pass into the rough ER, where they are folded into their working shapes.
questions.memoryHook: Rough ER is rough because ribosomes stud it.

questions.question: What is osmosis?
questions.correctAnswer: The movement of water across a membrane from high to low concentration
distractors: The movement of salt against a gradient
questions.explanation: Water moves through the membrane toward the side with more dissolved solute, evening out concentrations without the cell spending any energy.
questions.memoryHook: Water follows the salt in osmosis.

questions.question: What happens to a plant cell placed in pure water?
questions.correctAnswer: Water enters and the cell becomes turgid
distractors: Water leaves and the cell shrinks
questions.explanation: Water moves into the cell by osmosis; the cell wall prevents bursting, so the cell becomes firm.
questions.memoryHook: The cell wall stops a plant cell from popping.

questions.question: What is active transport?
questions.correctAnswer: Moving molecules against their gradient using energy
questions.explanation: Active transport uses ATP to move substances from low to high concentration.
questions.memoryHook: Active transport spends energy to push uphill.

questions.question: Which molecule carries genetic instructions for making proteins?
questions.correctAnswer: DNA
questions.explanation: DNA stores the instructions for building proteins in its base sequence.
questions.memoryHook: DNA is the recipe book for proteins.

questions.question: What is the cell theory?
questions.correctAnswer: All living things are made of cells, and cells come from other cells
distractors: Cells are the largest unit of life
Cells are made of atoms only
questions.explanation: Cell theory has three parts: the cell is the basic unit of life, all living things are made of one or more cells, and all cells arise from pre-existing cells.
questions.memoryHook: Every cell comes from another cell.

questions.question: Which organelle stores water and nutrients in a plant cell?
questions.correctAnswer: The central vacuole
questions.explanation: When the central vacuole fills with water, it presses the cell contents against the wall; this turgor pressure is what keeps stems and leaves standing upright.
questions.memoryHook: The vacuole is a plant cell's water tank.

questions.question: What is diffusion?
questions.correctAnswer: Movement of molecules from high to low concentration
questions.explanation: Diffusion needs no energy: constant random motion spreads particles from where they are crowded to where they are sparse, which is how oxygen crosses into the blood in the lungs.
questions.memoryHook: Diffusion spreads things from crowded to empty.

questions.question: What is the role of ATP in a cell?
questions.correctAnswer: To store and release energy for cell work
questions.explanation: ATP is the cell's energy currency, releasing energy when its bonds break.
questions.memoryHook: ATP is the cell's rechargeable battery.

questions.question: Which cells have a nucleus?
questions.correctAnswer: Eukaryotic cells
questions.explanation: Only eukaryotic cells keep their DNA inside a membrane-bound nucleus; bacteria and archaea are prokaryotic and have no nucleus at all.
questions.memoryHook: Eukaryotic means true nucleus.

questions.question: What is the function of the smooth endoplasmic reticulum?
questions.correctAnswer: To make lipids and detoxify chemicals
questions.explanation: With no ribosomes on its surface, the smooth ER builds lipids and steroid hormones and neutralizes alcohol and other toxins, especially in liver cells.
questions.memoryHook: Smooth ER makes fats and cleans up toxins.

questions.question: What is a stem cell?
questions.correctAnswer: An unspecialized cell that can develop into different cell types
questions.explanation: Stem cells can divide and differentiate into specialized cells.
questions.memoryHook: Stem cells are the body's blank slates.

questions.question: What is the main component of the cell membrane?
questions.correctAnswer: A phospholipid bilayer
questions.explanation: The membrane is two layers of phospholipids with proteins embedded.
questions.memoryHook: The membrane is a double layer of fats.

questions.question: Which organelle contains enzymes that break down hydrogen peroxide?
questions.correctAnswer: The peroxisome
questions.explanation: Peroxisomes break down fatty acids and detoxify hydrogen peroxide.
questions.memoryHook: Peroxisomes neutralize a toxic byproduct.

questions.question: What is a gene?
questions.correctAnswer: A segment of DNA that codes for a protein
questions.explanation: Most genes spell out the amino-acid sequence of one protein, and switching a gene on or off changes what a cell is able to do.
questions.memoryHook: A gene is a recipe for one protein.

questions.question: How many chromosomes do human body cells have?
questions.explanation: Human body cells are diploid: 23 chromosomes come from each parent, giving 46 in 23 homologous pairs; gametes carry only 23.
questions.memoryHook: Humans have 46 chromosomes.

questions.question: What are the four bases of DNA?
questions.correctAnswer: Adenine, thymine, cytosine, guanine
questions.explanation: The DNA bases are adenine, thymine, cytosine, and guanine; RNA uses the same set except that uracil replaces thymine.
questions.memoryHook: A pairs with T, C pairs with G.

questions.question: What does DNA stand for?
questions.correctAnswer: Deoxyribonucleic acid
questions.explanation: The name describes the molecule itself: a nucleic acid built from the sugar deoxyribose, phosphate groups, and nitrogen bases.
questions.memoryHook: DNA is deoxyribonucleic acid.

questions.question: In DNA, adenine always pairs with which base?
questions.correctAnswer: Thymine
questions.explanation: Base pairing is fixed by hydrogen bonds: adenine always bonds with thymine, and cytosine always bonds with guanine.
questions.memoryHook: A always hugs T.

questions.question: What is the shape of a DNA molecule?
questions.correctAnswer: A double helix
questions.explanation: A DNA molecule is two strands wound around each other like a twisted ladder, with sugar-phosphate rails and base-pair rungs.
questions.memoryHook: DNA twists like a ladder into a helix.

questions.question: What is a dominant allele?
questions.correctAnswer: An allele that is expressed when present in one copy
distractors: An allele that is never expressed
An allele found only in males
questions.explanation: A dominant allele shows its trait even when paired with a recessive allele.
questions.memoryHook: Dominant alleles show up with just one copy.

questions.question: What is the genotype of a heterozygous individual for a trait with alleles A and a?
questions.correctAnswer: Aa
questions.explanation: Heterozygous means the two alleles differ - one dominant (written with a capital A) and one recessive (lowercase a); AA and aa are homozygous instead.
questions.memoryHook: Hetero means different, so Aa.

questions.question: What is the probability that two heterozygous parents (Aa x Aa) have a child with genotype aa?
questions.explanation: A Punnett square gives AA, Aa, Aa, aa, so aa has a 1/4 chance.
questions.memoryHook: The Punnett square shows one aa in four.

questions.question: Who is known as the father of genetics?
questions.correctAnswer: Gregor Mendel
questions.explanation: Mendel's pea plant experiments in the 1800s revealed the laws of inheritance.
questions.memoryHook: Mendel counted peas and found the laws of heredity.

questions.question: What is a phenotype?
questions.correctAnswer: The observable traits of an organism
questions.explanation: Phenotype is the physical expression of the genotype, such as eye color.
questions.memoryHook: Phenotype is what you see.

questions.question: What is a mutation?
questions.correctAnswer: A change in the DNA sequence
questions.explanation: Mutations range from a single swapped base to whole missing segments, and a changed sequence can change the protein a gene builds.
questions.memoryHook: A mutation is a typo in the DNA.

questions.question: What is RNA's role in protein synthesis?
questions.correctAnswer: To carry instructions from DNA to the ribosome
distractors: To store genetic information long term
questions.explanation: Messenger RNA carries the DNA code to ribosomes, where proteins are built.
questions.memoryHook: MRNA is the messenger from DNA to the ribosome.

questions.question: In RNA, which base replaces thymine?
questions.correctAnswer: Uracil
questions.explanation: In RNA, uracil takes thymine's place and pairs with adenine, exactly as thymine does in DNA.
questions.memoryHook: RNA swaps T for U.

questions.question: What is meiosis?
questions.correctAnswer: Cell division that produces four gametes with half the chromosomes
distractors: Cell division that produces two identical cells
questions.explanation: Meiosis uses two divisions to turn one diploid cell into four haploid gametes, each carrying half the usual chromosome number.
questions.memoryHook: Meiosis halves the chromosomes for sex cells.

questions.question: What is mitosis?
questions.correctAnswer: Cell division that produces two identical body cells
distractors: The fusion of egg and sperm
questions.explanation: Mitosis uses a single division to turn one cell into two daughter cells, each keeping the full set of 46 chromosomes.
questions.memoryHook: Mitosis copies cells for growth and repair.

questions.question: What is a sex-linked trait?
questions.correctAnswer: A trait carried on a sex chromosome
distractors: A trait found only in females
questions.explanation: Because the gene sits on a sex chromosome, inheritance follows sex: males, who have only one X chromosome, show X-linked recessive traits such as color blindness far more often.
questions.memoryHook: Color blindness rides on the X chromosome.

questions.question: What does a Punnett square show?
questions.correctAnswer: The possible genotypes of offspring from a cross
distractors: The actual children of a couple
The order of genes on a chromosome
questions.explanation: Each parent supplies one allele to the boxes, so a Punnett square gives the genotype ratios to expect in offspring - probabilities, not guarantees.
questions.memoryHook: A Punnett square predicts the possible kids.

questions.question: What is codominance?
questions.correctAnswer: When both alleles are fully expressed in the heterozygote
distractors: When one allele hides the other
questions.explanation: In codominance, both alleles show, as in AB blood type.
questions.memoryHook: AB blood shows both A and B.

questions.question: What is incomplete dominance?
questions.correctAnswer: When the heterozygote shows a blend of the two traits
distractors: When one allele is fully dominant
questions.explanation: In incomplete dominance, a red and white flower cross gives pink offspring.
questions.memoryHook: Pink flowers are a blend of red and white.

questions.question: What is the process of copying DNA called?
questions.correctAnswer: Replication
questions.explanation: In replication, enzymes unwind the double helix and build a new matching strand on each old strand, producing two identical DNA molecules.
questions.memoryHook: Replication copies DNA.

questions.question: What is transcription?
questions.correctAnswer: Copying a DNA sequence into RNA
questions.explanation: In transcription, the enzyme RNA polymerase reads one strand of a gene's DNA and assembles a matching messenger RNA copy.
questions.memoryHook: Transcription writes DNA into RNA.

questions.question: What is translation?
questions.correctAnswer: Building a protein from an mRNA code at the ribosome
questions.explanation: Translation reads mRNA codons and assembles amino acids into a protein.
questions.memoryHook: Translation turns the RNA message into a protein.

questions.question: What is a codon?
questions.correctAnswer: A three-base sequence on mRNA that codes for an amino acid
questions.explanation: The ribosome reads mRNA three bases at a time, and each codon matches a transfer RNA carrying one specific amino acid.
questions.memoryHook: Three letters of mRNA code for one amino acid.

questions.question: What is Down syndrome caused by?
questions.correctAnswer: An extra copy of chromosome 21
questions.explanation: Down syndrome usually comes from nondisjunction: an egg or sperm keeps two copies of chromosome 21, so after fertilization the cells have three - trisomy 21.
questions.memoryHook: Down syndrome is an extra chromosome 21.

questions.question: What is natural selection?
questions.correctAnswer: The process by which organisms with helpful traits survive and reproduce more
distractors: The random movement of genes only
questions.explanation: Natural selection favors traits that improve survival and reproduction in an environment.
questions.memoryHook: Nature selects the traits that work best.

questions.question: Who proposed the theory of evolution by natural selection?
questions.correctAnswer: Charles Darwin
questions.explanation: Darwin published On the Origin of Species in 1859, proposing natural selection.
questions.memoryHook: Darwin's finches revealed natural selection.

questions.question: What is a fossil?
questions.correctAnswer: The preserved remains or traces of an ancient organism
questions.explanation: Fossils form when dead organisms are buried in sediment that hardens into rock, preserving bones, shells, or even footprints for millions of years.
questions.memoryHook: Fossils are echoes of ancient life.

questions.question: What is adaptation?
questions.correctAnswer: A trait that helps an organism survive in its environment
questions.explanation: An adaptation is an inherited trait that improves survival or reproduction.
questions.memoryHook: Camouflage is an adaptation.

questions.question: What is speciation?
questions.correctAnswer: The formation of a new species
questions.explanation: Speciation occurs when populations become reproductively isolated and diverge.
questions.memoryHook: New species form when populations split apart.

questions.question: What is genetic drift?
questions.correctAnswer: Random changes in allele frequencies in a population
questions.explanation: Genetic drift is chance change in gene frequencies, strongest in small populations.
questions.memoryHook: Genetic drift is evolution by luck.

questions.question: What is the main source of new genetic variation?
questions.correctAnswer: Mutation
questions.explanation: Mutations create new alleles, the raw material for evolution.
questions.memoryHook: Mutations create new genetic options.

questions.question: What is a homologous structure?
questions.correctAnswer: A structure in different species with a common evolutionary origin
distractors: A structure with the same function but different origin
A structure that has no function
A structure found in only one species
questions.explanation: Homologous structures, like the forelimbs of humans and bats, share an ancestor.
questions.memoryHook: A bat wing and a human arm share a blueprint.

questions.question: What is a vestigial structure?
questions.correctAnswer: A structure that has lost most of its original function
distractors: A structure that is fully functional
A new structure in a species
A structure found in fossils only
questions.explanation: Vestigial structures, like the human appendix, are reduced remnants of once-useful features.
questions.memoryHook: The appendix is a leftover from our ancestors.

questions.question: What is an ecosystem?
questions.correctAnswer: A community of organisms interacting with their physical environment
distractors: A group of the same animals
questions.explanation: An ecosystem includes living organisms plus the nonliving factors they interact with.
questions.memoryHook: An ecosystem is life plus its surroundings.

questions.question: What is a producer in an ecosystem?
questions.correctAnswer: An organism that makes its own food, usually by photosynthesis
distractors: An organism that eats other animals
An organism that breaks down dead matter
questions.explanation: Producers, like plants and algae, make food from sunlight.
questions.memoryHook: Producers make the food everyone else eats.

questions.question: What is a decomposer?
questions.correctAnswer: An organism that breaks down dead matter and returns nutrients to the soil
distractors: An organism that eats only seeds
questions.explanation: Decomposers like fungi and bacteria recycle nutrients from dead organisms.
questions.memoryHook: Decomposers recycle the dead into soil.

questions.question: What is a food chain?
questions.correctAnswer: A sequence showing who eats whom in an ecosystem
questions.explanation: A food chain traces energy from producers through consumers.
questions.memoryHook: A food chain shows energy passing from eater to eaten.

questions.question: What is carrying capacity?
questions.correctAnswer: The largest population an environment can support long term
distractors: The number of predators in an area
The birth rate of a species
questions.explanation: A population grows until food, space, water, or predators limit it; that ceiling is the carrying capacity, the flat top of a logistic S-shaped growth curve.
questions.memoryHook: Carrying capacity is the environment's limit.

questions.question: What is symbiosis?
questions.correctAnswer: A close, long-term interaction between two species
questions.explanation: Symbiosis is the umbrella term for close, long-term living arrangements between species - mutualism, commensalism, and parasitism are its three main forms.
questions.memoryHook: Symbiosis is living closely together.

questions.question: What is mutualism?
questions.correctAnswer: A symbiotic relationship where both species benefit
distractors: A relationship where one benefits and one is harmed
A relationship where one benefits and one is unaffected
A relationship where both are harmed
questions.explanation: In mutualism, both partners gain, like bees and flowers.
questions.memoryHook: Bees and flowers both win.

questions.question: What is parasitism?
questions.correctAnswer: A relationship where one organism benefits and the other is harmed
questions.explanation: A parasite lives on or in a host, gaining food while harming the host.
questions.memoryHook: A parasite takes and the host pays.

questions.question: What is competition in ecology?
questions.correctAnswer: Organisms fighting for the same limited resources
questions.explanation: Competition occurs when organisms need the same resources, like food or space.
questions.memoryHook: Two species wanting the same food compete.

questions.question: What is a keystone species?
questions.correctAnswer: A species whose presence strongly affects the whole ecosystem
questions.explanation: Removing a keystone species causes major changes throughout the ecosystem.
questions.memoryHook: Sea otters are a keystone species in kelp forests.

questions.question: What is biodiversity?
questions.correctAnswer: The variety of life in an area, including species diversity
distractors: The number of humans in an area
questions.explanation: Biodiversity is the variety of genes, species, and ecosystems in a place.
questions.memoryHook: Biodiversity is life's variety.

questions.question: What is the main cause of the greenhouse effect?
questions.correctAnswer: Gases like carbon dioxide trapping heat in the atmosphere
questions.explanation: Greenhouse gases absorb and re-emit heat, warming the Earth.
questions.memoryHook: CO2 traps heat like a blanket.

questions.question: What is a trophic level?
questions.correctAnswer: A feeding level in a food chain or web
questions.explanation: Trophic levels are the steps in a food chain: producers, herbivores, carnivores.
questions.memoryHook: Each trophic level is one step up the food chain.

questions.question: What is succession?
questions.correctAnswer: The gradual change in species over time in an area
questions.explanation: Ecological succession is the orderly replacement of species in a community over time.
questions.memoryHook: A bare field slowly becomes a forest.

questions.question: What is a biome?
questions.correctAnswer: A large region with a distinct climate and characteristic organisms
questions.explanation: Biomes, like deserts and rainforests, are large areas defined by climate and life.
questions.memoryHook: A desert is a biome.

questions.question: What is the role of nitrogen-fixing bacteria?
questions.correctAnswer: To convert nitrogen gas into forms plants can use
questions.explanation: Nitrogen-fixing bacteria turn atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia and nitrates for plants.
questions.memoryHook: Bacteria make nitrogen usable for plants.

questions.question: What is the function of red blood cells?
questions.correctAnswer: To carry oxygen around the body
questions.explanation: Red blood cells are packed with hemoglobin, which picks up oxygen in the lungs and releases it in the tissues; they have no nucleus, leaving more room for hemoglobin.
questions.memoryHook: Red blood cells deliver oxygen.

questions.question: What is the function of white blood cells?
questions.correctAnswer: To fight infections and disease
questions.explanation: White blood cells patrol the blood and tissues, engulfing microbes and producing antibodies; unlike red blood cells, they keep their nucleus.
questions.memoryHook: White blood cells are the immune system's soldiers.

questions.question: Which organ pumps blood around the body?
questions.correctAnswer: The heart
questions.explanation: With each beat, the heart's ventricles squeeze blood into the arteries - oxygen-rich blood to the body and oxygen-poor blood to the lungs.
questions.memoryHook: The heart is the body's pump.

questions.question: What is the main function of the lungs?
questions.correctAnswer: To exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: In the lungs' alveoli, oxygen diffuses into the blood while carbon dioxide diffuses out to be exhaled; the diaphragm muscle drives the breathing itself.
questions.memoryHook: Lungs swap oxygen for carbon dioxide.

questions.question: What is photosynthesis?
questions.correctAnswer: The process by which plants make food using sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide
distractors: The process by which animals make energy
The movement of water in plants
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis uses light energy to build glucose from water and carbon dioxide.
questions.memoryHook: Photosynthesis turns light into sugar.

questions.question: What is cellular respiration?
questions.correctAnswer: The process that releases energy from glucose using oxygen
distractors: The process of making food in plants
The exchange of gases in the lungs
questions.explanation: Cellular respiration breaks down glucose to release energy as ATP.
questions.memoryHook: Respiration burns sugar for energy.

questions.question: What is the chemical equation for photosynthesis?
questions.correctAnswer: 6CO2 + 6H2O + light energy -> C6H12O6 + 6O2
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis combines carbon dioxide and water with light to make glucose and oxygen.
questions.memoryHook: Photosynthesis builds sugar from air and water.

questions.question: Which pigment captures light in photosynthesis?
questions.correctAnswer: Chlorophyll
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll in chloroplasts absorbs sunlight, mostly red and blue light.
questions.memoryHook: Chlorophyll makes plants green.

questions.question: Where does photosynthesis take place?
questions.correctAnswer: In the chloroplasts of plant cells
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis runs in the chloroplasts of mesophyll cells inside leaves, close to the light and to the veins that deliver water.
questions.memoryHook: Chloroplasts are the kitchen of the leaf.

questions.question: What is the main function of the roots of a plant?
questions.correctAnswer: To absorb water and minerals from the soil
questions.explanation: Roots anchor the plant and absorb water and nutrients.
questions.memoryHook: Roots drink for the plant.

questions.question: What is the function of the xylem in a plant?
questions.correctAnswer: To transport water and minerals upward
questions.explanation: Xylem is built from dead, hollow vessel cells stacked into tubes; evaporation from the leaves pulls water up these tubes from the roots.
questions.memoryHook: Xylem carries water up.

questions.question: What is the function of the phloem in a plant?
questions.correctAnswer: To transport food (sugars) throughout the plant
questions.explanation: Phloem is living tissue that moves sugars from sources, where they are made (leaves), to sinks, where they are used or stored (roots, fruits, seeds).
questions.memoryHook: Phloem delivers the food.

questions.question: What is the role of stomata in leaves?
questions.correctAnswer: To allow gas exchange and control water loss
questions.explanation: Stomata are pores that let carbon dioxide in and oxygen and water vapor out.
questions.memoryHook: Stomata are the leaf's breathing pores.

questions.question: What is the nervous system's main job?
questions.correctAnswer: To receive, process, and respond to information
questions.explanation: Sensory neurons detect stimuli, interneurons in the brain and spinal cord process the signals, and motor neurons trigger the response in muscles or glands.
questions.memoryHook: Nerves carry the body's messages.

questions.question: What is a neuron?
questions.correctAnswer: A nerve cell that carries electrical signals
questions.explanation: A neuron's dendrites receive signals and its long axon carries the electrical impulse onward to other cells; ordinary body cells cannot pass signals this way.
questions.memoryHook: Neurons are the wires of the nervous system.

questions.question: What is homeostasis?
questions.correctAnswer: The maintenance of a stable internal environment
questions.explanation: Homeostasis keeps conditions like temperature and blood sugar steady.
questions.memoryHook: Homeostasis keeps the body's balance.

questions.question: Which organ filters blood and makes urine?
questions.correctAnswer: The kidney
questions.explanation: Inside each kidney, about a million nephrons filter blood under pressure, reabsorbing the water and salts the body needs and sending the waste out as urine.
questions.memoryHook: Kidneys filter the blood.

questions.question: What is the function of the liver?
questions.correctAnswer: To process nutrients, detoxify blood, and make bile
questions.explanation: The liver processes nutrients, breaks down toxins, and produces bile for digestion.
questions.memoryHook: The liver is the body's chemical factory.

questions.question: What hormone lowers blood sugar?
questions.correctAnswer: Insulin
questions.explanation: Insulin, made by the pancreas, helps cells take in glucose and lowers blood sugar.
questions.memoryHook: Insulin opens the door for sugar to enter cells.

questions.question: What is the function of the skeleton?
questions.correctAnswer: To support the body, protect organs, and produce blood cells
questions.explanation: Bones support the body, protect organs, and make blood cells in marrow.
questions.memoryHook: Bones support, protect, and make blood.

questions.question: What is the main function of the digestive system?
questions.correctAnswer: To break down food and absorb nutrients
questions.explanation: Churning and enzymes break food into molecules small enough to pass through the intestinal wall into the blood.
questions.memoryHook: Digestion turns food into fuel.

questions.question: Which enzyme in saliva begins breaking down starch?
questions.correctAnswer: Amylase
questions.explanation: Amylase in saliva starts digesting starch into sugars.
questions.memoryHook: Amylase starts digesting starch in your mouth.

questions.question: What is the function of the immune system?
questions.correctAnswer: To defend the body against pathogens
questions.explanation: The immune system recognizes and attacks invaders like bacteria and viruses.
questions.memoryHook: The immune system is the body's defense force.

questions.question: What is a pathogen?
questions.correctAnswer: A microorganism that causes disease
distractors: A type of white blood cell
questions.explanation: Most microbes are harmless or even helpful; pathogens are the minority of microorganisms that invade the body and cause disease.
questions.memoryHook: Pathogens are germs that make you sick.

questions.question: What is an enzyme?
questions.correctAnswer: A protein that speeds up chemical reactions
questions.explanation: Enzymes act as biological catalysts, speeding reactions without being used up.
questions.memoryHook: Enzymes speed up reactions without being used up.
